newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Interroll plans to sell majority in IPO.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Interroll plans to sell majority in IPO.

text.p: Interroll Holding AG said its three founding families had decided to sell a majority of the company in an Initial Public Offering (IPO).
Interroll, which makes conveyor belt and rolling transport systems, said the price of its new shares would be determined after the bookbuilding process.
From May 26 to June 3 are invited to place their offers within a certain price range, the company added in a statement.
The first day of trading is planned for June 5.

Union Bank of Switzerland said in a recent study on Interroll that in connection with the IPO the company would introduce a single registered share with a nominal value of 50 Swiss francs. A total of 854,000 shares will be created.
UBS also said 50 to 60 percent of Interroll's share capital and votes will be listed and the price of the shares and the allocation would be determined on June 4.
The three families Specht, vom Stein and Ghisalberti currently hold 65.3 percent of Interroll's shares. After the IPO, UBS said they will own a total of 30-36 percent.
